html:
SMTO-SKL-0111 — Your Slack app setup in Parameter Store isn't valid

GUID: a24fc926-53ab-5489-861a-8062751a3b0b
Slug: slack-oauth-app-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • The saved Slack OAuth App entry is missing something or has a value Slack sign-in can't use, such as the wrong return address or no permissions chosen. SMTO didn't contact Slack.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu, open your Slack OAuth App entry, and check the client ID (two numbers joined by a dot) and client secret match your Slack app's settings. Slack won't accept a sign-in from an app whose ID or secret is missing or mistyped.
  2. Check redirect_uri starts with https:// and ends with /api/agent/slack/oauth/callback, and that the same address is registered in your Slack app. Slack only sends you back to a secure address registered for the app, and SMTO listens only at that path.
  3. Check the permissions: with flow user, choose at least one user scope and no bot scopes; with flow workspace, choose at least one bot scope. users:read.email also needs users:read. SMTO refuses permission choices that don't fit the kind of connection you picked.
  4. Save the entry, then ask SMTO to connect Slack again. SMTO checks the app entry each time a connection starts, so the corrected version is used.

What success looks like

  • SMTO gives you a Slack sign-in link, and Slack's page lists the permissions you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. The details don't say which field is wrong, to keep secrets out of them, so they may need to check the entry with you. Never share the client secret.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The slack_oauth_app profile fails validation: wrong type or version, a missing or malformed field, a redirect_uri that is not HTTPS with path /api/agent/slack/oauth/callback, or a scope selection that does not fit its flow.

What this means

  • Slack app profile type/version or fields fail the supported OAuth profile schema. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack app profile type/version or fields fail the supported OAuth profile schema.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the app schema, registered callback and deliberate user/bot scope configuration without exposing secrets.

How to fix it

  • Fix the slack_oauth_app record (parameter_profiles.validate): client_id must match digits.digits, client_secret must be a single non-empty line, redirect_uri must be https with no query, fragment or credentials and path exactly /api/agent/slack/oauth/callback. flow "user" needs requested_user_scopes and no bot scopes; flow "workspace" needs requested_bot_scopes; search:read is not allowed as a bot scope or chat:write.public as a user scope; users:read.email requires users:read and chat:write.public requires chat:write. Register the same callback in the Slack app.
  • Use a Slack client ID and secret, explicit user or bot scopes, and a registered HTTPS callback ending /api/agent/slack/oauth/callback.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended app profile validates and matches its registered callback.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
